day_shape: 87 items: Iran says four oil tankers hit by explosions in Strait of Hormuz and Sirik struck by 'enemy' fire, IDF confirms Nasser Hospital strike on Hamas Khan Younis commander, Trump pulls Vance off Iran file, two convicted in London of spying on Iran International, UK FCDO statements on Gaza and Yemen sanctions, heavy Khamenei Fatimiyyah mourning cycle.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents
threads.summary: Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings, and Iranian sources told IRNA that Sirik in Hormozgan was struck by 'an enemy'. Defa Press attributed successive explosions near Sirik to warning shots at 'violating vessels', while ex-Mossad chief David Barnea told the Jerusalem Post an extended Hormuz blockade was the best option to stop Iran's nuclear programme.

threads.label: Nasser Hospital strike on Hamas commander
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said an overnight strike on the Nasser Hospital complex in Khan Younis targeted Khan Younis Brigade commander Muhammad Abu Ismail, with Hamas authorities reporting six killed and at least 20 wounded. A separate Israeli strike was reported near Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, and the IDF said the Nasser second floor served as a Hamas HQ where hostages had been held.

threads.label: Trump sidelines Vance from Iran file
threads.summary: Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to focus on alleged Democratic corruption rather than Iran negotiations, saying Washington no longer needed a deal and the Iranian regime was collapsing. Iran International and IRIB linked the move to Vance attributing Republican midterm losses to the prolonged war with Iran; House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries called for 'dramatic change' in US policy toward Israel and an end to the Iran war.

threads.label: Iran nuclear and missile posture
threads.summary: Iran's Assembly of Experts became the first governing body to call for review of the country's defence doctrine, potentially opening the religious ban on nuclear weapons, while a Jerusalem Post-cited intelligence estimate put Iran's ballistic missile production at roughly 50 per month. Israel's security cabinet is set to meet Sunday for the first time in six weeks amid IDF preparations for possible renewed strikes, and senior IRGC officials issued fresh threats to kill US and Israeli leaders.

threads.label: UK and UN action on Yemen and Gaza
threads.summary: UK Permanent Representative Sarah MacIntosh delivered the UK explanation of vote as the Security Council renewed the 2140 Yemen sanctions regime until 14 November 2027, and read a multi-country Call to Action joint statement on health and humanitarian access into Gaza. Minister Stephen Doughty gave a Commons statement on Gaza, while the Jerusalem Post reported Saudi Arabia is pressing the EU to designate the Houthis as terrorists against European peace-process concerns.

threads.label: Iranian covert operations in Europe
threads.summary: Two Iranian men were convicted at London's Woolwich Crown Court of assisting Iranian intelligence operations targeting Iran International journalists in Britain, after a six-week trial. ITV News reported a seven-man Iran-linked network helped coordinate attacks across Europe using local criminals and AI-generated propaganda to target Jewish communities.

threads.label: Khamenei Fatimiyyah mourning cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted heavily from the Zaynabiyyah mourning ceremony for the night of Fatima al-Zahra's martyrdom, led by the Supreme Leader near the grave of the 'martyred leader of Iran'. Defa Press and IRIB carried accompanying coverage including an invitation to funeral processions for 110 and 350 'unknown martyrs', remarks by Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani, and Kayhan editor Shariatmadari's claims that the US had been defeated by Iran.
